description: What each bus of the controller carries, in a form a program can read: the bit timing the firmware sets, the frame format, the identifier window of a slot and the identifiers of the relay protocol. tests/test_bus_contract.py compares it with the firmware sources and with tools/can_ids.py, so a change in one of them that is not made here fails the tests. The bit rate is derived from the timing and from the kernel clock the firmware assumes; no board has measured it yet.

stack_a.name: STACK A (FDCAN1 of the kinematic brain to FDCAN1 of every controller board)

tool_head_downlink.name: Tier 2 downlink (FDCAN2 of a controller board to its tool head)

cm5_spi.name: SPI link between the CM5 and the STM32H745

slot_messages: see tools/can_ids.py: each message is an offset inside the 32-identifier window of a slot; the identifier is slot_base + slot * slot_window + offset
data_length_per_message: not yet recorded: only the classic maximum of 8 bytes is a contract today

emergency_stop.status: firmware written and tested on the host (estop_can.h, estop_brain.h, relay of the controller board, STACK A task of the brain); nothing has run on a board

frame.format: classic data frame, 11-bit identifier, no remote frame

emergency_stop.timing_note: proposals to be confirmed on the bench (docs/BENCH_TESTS.md rows 17, 18, 20 and 21); they move to the configuration file of the machine when the firmware reads them
emergency_stop.stop_category: 0 (drivers off at once) until the owner decides otherwise per axis

slot_scan.status: firmware of the controller board answers the probe (bootloader and application, slot_scan_node.h) and is tested on the host; the host client that sends it is not written and nothing has run on a board
slot_scan.timing_note: proposals to be confirmed on the bench (docs/BENCH_TESTS.md row 15); they move to the configuration file of the machine when the firmware reads them
